entry.summary:
# Agent N's Hermes News — September 24, 2026

Executive Summary

This week's headline is the Bot Screen launch: @NousResearch unveiled real-time screen streaming for Hermes Desktop, and Teknium followed with live visual/interactive desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent — you can now watch, and even interact with, the same machine your agent controls. Under the hood, Hermes Agent v0.21.4 shipped with 1,812 merged PRs and a new --format stream-json flag that powers the newly documented Hermes–Claude plugin pipeline, which drives the unmodified official Claude Code CLI while keeping all credentials in the CLI's own login flow. Around the ecosystem, Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 hardened MCP security, rlaope open-sourced jeval and expanded oh-my-hermes, and the alpha-stage AgentProto v0.20.0 runtime arrived for multi-agent orchestration.

Releases

  • Bot Screen for Hermes Desktop — live streaming of any agent session, now official. Paired with desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent, users can watch and interact with the machine their agent is driving. Official docs are live.
  • Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (tagged v2026.9.21, released 21 September) — adds a --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL for scriptable pipelines. This release underpins the new Claude plugin pipeline and broader CLI automation use cases.
  • Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 — hardens MCP with per-invocation session scoping plus identity/origin checks.
  • AgentProto v0.20.0 (Apache-2.0, released 22 September) — a new TypeScript runtime that orchestrates multiple coding agents, including Hermes, from a single scheduler. Alpha maturity: expect rough edges.

Merged PRs

  • Hermes Agent v0.21.4 bundled 1,812 merged PRs. Standouts:
  • Skills auto-load — skills now load automatically.
  • Configurable MCP discovery concurrency — tune how aggressively MCP discovery runs in parallel.

Community

  • Bot Screen launch reception — euphoric and long-awaited. The launch thread drew roughly 173k views; Teknium's "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" (~20k views) captured the pent-up demand. @tonbistudio published a community walkthrough alongside the official docs.
  • OMH + Jev ecosystem — rlaope delivered the batch's strongest organic engagement (1,706 views) announcing oh-my-hermes (OMH) support for Jev-Skills and model routing, then open-sourced jeval (Jev evaluation/visualization) and shipped an updated oh-my-hermes Plus — positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for AI-native hermes-agent power users.
  • Hands-on maintenance — Teknium stayed visible: disputing a cache complaint pending a reproducible issue, celebrating a quick "fixed lol" resolution, and clarifying that a tool under discussion was built by the Nous/Hermes team, not Anthropic.
  • Broader chatter — a lukewarm take praising Opus 5.5 while questioning Claude Code's agent experience, GitHub show-and-tell prompts, and short reaction posts capped a launch-driven week.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Hermes via iMessage — the official account's practical gem: use Hermes through iMessage with whichever model you prefer (~13k views).
  • Claude plugin pipeline, explained — a deep engineering walkthrough shows Hermes driving the unmodified official Claude Code CLI over stream-json. A companion security doc confirms authentication lives entirely in the CLI's claude auth login flow — Hermes never handles or stores API keys.
  • Watching your agents work — pair Bot Screen streaming with desktop passthrough; the official docs plus the @tonbistudio walkthrough are the fastest way in.

entry.title: Research Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: This week's research is anchored by the Hermes–Claude subscription plugin: a deep engineering walkthrough of the pipeline — Hermes drives the unmodified official Claude Code CLI over stream-json — paired with a security-focused companion doc showing auth lives entirely in the official CLI's claude auth login flow, so no API keys or credentials are handled or stored by Hermes itself. Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (tagged v2026.9.21, released 21 Sept) adds a new --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL for scriptable pipelines, bundled with 1,812 merged PRs including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency. Broader ecosystem releases round out the section: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 hardens MCP security with per-invocation session scoping and identity/origin checks, and the new open-source runtime AgentProto v0.20.0 (Apache-2.0) orchestrates multiple coding agents — including Hermes — signaling growing interop despite its alpha maturity. Practical takeaway: Hermes users get safer credential handling, scriptable CLI automation, and an ecosystem converging on hardened, interoperable agent tooling.
